socials.reason: Exam graphs, sources, innovation cards and written reasoning need selectable evidence and answer feedback. The 3D exam desk is presentation, not a spatial learning target.

world.reason: Country bubbles encode data over time; losing axes, sliders and data provenance in native AR would undermine the comparison task. Keep the live chart in the browser.

read.reason: Reading-comprehension evidence selection and written answers are the learning task; a physical prop would not add spatial understanding.

words.reason: Vocabulary, language choices and written explanations require readable text and feedback rather than a placed object.

essay.reason: Planning and assessing essay structure depends on text editing and comparison; no native object is proposed.

maps.reason: The lesson compares mapped distributions and development indicators; an unlabelled map mesh would lose the evidence and controls needed for interpretation.

market.reason: Supply, demand, price and quantity are explored through changing graphs; a static AR prop would not preserve the economic relationships.

ai.reason: The lesson’s learning task is reasoning about AI and evaluating outputs, not inspecting a physical machine; keep its interactive evidence and explanations.

lines.reason: Linear relationships depend on draggable coordinates, equations and readable axes. A detached static 3D snapshot would remove the key feedback.

civics.reason: Government structures, decisions and civic reasoning need labelled relationships and explanation; no arbitrary AR building or desk is added.

data.reason: Statistical interpretation relies on readable values, distributions and comparisons; keep the live browser charts and questions.

quote.reason: Quote-to-point is English paragraph construction: claim, textual evidence, explanation and significance. Its editable text and self-check rubric are the learning task; a native prop would add no spatial understanding.

queue.reason: Queue probability needs arrivals, service timing and repeated trials. A static counter scene would misrepresent the learning process.

claims.reason: Evaluating a claim requires its evidence, source and explanation. No spatial object is necessary for that task.

algebra.reason: Equation manipulation and immediate symbolic feedback are central; placing an unrelated 3D object would not support the algebra task.

gradient.reason: Level 2 calculus uses a draggable tangent, derivative feedback and linked rates. The cyclist, seedling and tank are contexts; a static export would lose the relationships being taught.

gradient3.reason: Same gradient route at level=3: product/chain/trig/log derivatives and inflection points still depend on live tangent and symbolic feedback. Classified web-first consistently with Level 2.

unseen.reason: Level 2 unseen-text work requires tagging technique, effect and idea against the text. The 3D desk is presentation only.

unseen3.reason: Same unseen route at level=3: technique, effect, position and evaluation still require the text and annotations. Classified web-first consistently with Level 2.

text.reason: Text interpretation and literary evidence must remain readable and selectable; no standalone spatial model is needed.

y9english.reason: Year 9 English reading and writing practice depends on text and feedback, not a physical AR prop.

inanga.reason: Restored īnanga spawning-bank cross-section: fenced, unmown and planted, at the lesson’s spring high tide. Native grass strip and tide marks are preserved; pink is spring and blue is neap high water. Miniature illustrative landscape, not geographic scale. Egg development and restoration comparisons remain live in the browser.

reactions.reason: Selected sealed flask before mixing marble chips with acid, including its inner vial. The plaque explains surface area and collision opportunities; this model supports apparatus inspection, not reaction-rate measurement. Miniature teaching apparatus; no native collisions, catalyst experiment or gas collection.

climate.reason: Only the authored surface-tile albedo comparison is selected: ice, ocean, forest, farm and city features. The native plaque explains the light/dark reflection comparison. This is a schematic, not Earth geography; moving radiation, greenhouse feedback and carbon-cycle calculations remain in the lesson.

fish.reason: The existing rod-lever investigation with a 2 kg load, 2.4 m rod and 0.5 m grip distance. Pivot, effort/load arrows and reference lines are retained with a native moment equation. Miniature static teaching diagram; force calculations and grip changes stay in the browser.

fly.reason: Aoraki / Mount Cook: bounded LINZ elevation relief, 170.03–170.25° E and 43.53–43.69° S. A 17.71 × 17.79 km region at horizontal 1:35,425, vertical 1:23,617 (1.5× exaggeration); terrain width 50 cm. Labels identify sampled high ridge and valley, north and 5 km scale. Bilinear 129×129 cartographic grid; maximum sample is not a surveyed summit. No buildings, trees, aerial imagery or current glacier boundaries. Static relief; flight controls stay in the browser. Elevation © LINZ, CC BY 4.0; cropped/resampled by assembl.

particles.reason: Only the heating station and its initial solid-water lattice are exported, not the separate gas syringe or mountain. Oxygen/hydrogen colours and the enlarged-molecule scale warning are retained. Apparatus and molecular dimensions intentionally use different scales; phase change, motion and temperature readouts remain in the lesson.

energy.reason: One selected heating apparatus: jug, coil, water and thermometer, initially 1 kg of water at 15°C with a 2.2 kW setting. The label relates E=Pt to mcΔT. Miniature teaching apparatus; no heating, boiling or live energy calculation in the native viewer.

kokopu.reason: The authored banded kōkopu in its low-water stream habitat: undercut bank, fern cover, log and grassy margin. A miniature habitat cross-section, not a field survey or measured fish replica. Daytime static snapshot; lateral-line sensing, flood timing and odour-choice experiments stay in the lesson.

ecology.reason: The existing 0–40 m shingle-beach transect, isolated from the separate energy pyramid. Quadrats are placed every 5 m; soil thickness is exaggerated. The native plaque retains the top-to-sea direction and plant-zone key. Miniature illustrative sampling layout; live graphs and food-web population changes remain in the browser.

sky.reason: The existing Earth–Moon geometry at the lesson’s initial 23 October 2026 NZDT state, with the tilted Earth axis and lunar orbit. Separate size/distance scales are declared on the model. Native environmental lighting does not reproduce solar illumination, phases, tides or seasons; use the browser for those investigations.

space.reason: Saturn and its authored ring geometry, isolated from the solar-system, HR and life-cycle views. Ring radii follow the lesson’s 1.11–2.35 Saturn-radius construction; the complete planet/rings display is resized to 50 cm. Procedural surface texture, not a photograph. Native environmental lighting does not reproduce the lesson’s solar shadows or orbital motion.

materials.reason: One existing electrical-conductivity test circuit with the copper sample selected at 20°C, isolated from six other test areas and molecular diagrams. The native key identifies battery, sample and lamp, and explains mobile electrons. Static miniature apparatus; changing materials and particle-state experiments remain in the browser.

plan.reason: The lesson’s initial emergency-department layout, with room labels embedded. The 30 m × 20 m interior is shown at 1:50 in plan; wall/slab heights are exaggerated. It intentionally remains the starting design, not an approved clinical layout or saved student revision. Dragging, alternative layouts and constraint checks stay in the lesson.
